Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.summary: Turn multi-factor authentication off

post.description: Requires the current password and a code from the authenticator (or a recovery code): new codes are a second factor, so a stolen session and password alone do not mint them. The old recovery codes stop working; the new ones are shown this once. 409 while MFA is not enabled.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.summary: Replace the recovery codes

post.description: Requires the current password (422 on current_password). Returns the secret and otpauth:// URI for an authenticator app; nothing changes for the login until POST /auth/mfa/totp/confirm gets a code from it. A new enrollment replaces one pending; 409 while MFA is enabled.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.summary: Begin enrolling a TOTP authenticator

post.description: A code from the authenticator just set up (mfa_code) enables multi-factor authentication: from then on a login needs mfa_code. Every other session of the user ends (they were started on the password alone); this one stays. Returns the recovery codes, shown this once. A wrong code is a 422 on mfa_code; 409 with no enrollment pending.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.summary: Confirm a TOTP enrollment and enable MFA

post.description: Requires the current password (a wrong one is a 422 on current_password). Signs out every other session of the user unless keep_other_sessions; this session stays. Outstanding password reset links stop working. Too many wrong current passwords is a 429 (Retry-After).

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.summary: Change the signed-in user's password

post.description: 202 with the same body whether or not the email is an account, answered before that is known: the message is sent in the background. 503 (Retry-After) when the server is taking no more reset requests for now, decided from request arrivals alone, also before the lookup. 429 (Retry-After) when this client address asked too often, also before the lookup. At most one message a minute per account; the link works once, until it expires.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.description: Requires the auth.users.manage permission (a superuser has it), and a superuser to disable a superuser; no one disables their own account (409). post.description: For a user who lost their authenticator and recovery codes; every session of the user ends with it (the lost device may hold one). Requires the auth.users.manage permission (a superuser has it), and a superuser to reset a superuser; an account turns its own off with POST /auth/mfa/disable (409). Idempotent.
